name: brainstorming
description: Use before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.

name: curating-requests
description: Use when a Slack message wakes the Intake routine and must be judged before it enters the factory. Turns it into one issue with origin slack in the project that owns it, points it at an existing issue, asks one question, or declines it politely, never twice for one Slack message.

name: deciding-issues
description: Decisions, the one way a factory run asks a person. Use when a run must stop for a ruling or a mockup, when its question is answered or expires, when Intake asks a reporter in Slack, or when a person starts a sitting to clear Paused issues.

name: diagnosing-bugs
description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

name: evaluating-changes
description: Trial of a change before it is trusted. Use when Land's judge tries a PR head, or a person asks for a pull request, a branch or a written spec to be judged. One juror, five counts in sequence, one ranked verdict, nothing written to the code.

name: executing-issues
description: Build stage. Use when the Build routine takes the next In progress issue of its pipe and turns it into a pull request on a green gate, or into a Decision that names what is missing.

name: filing-findings
description: Use when a scouting pass has candidates and must decide which of them get filed, as an issue with origin scout:<kind>. The shared cost, budget and ranking bar every scout obeys.

name: implement
description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.

name: importing-github-issues
description: Use once per repository at its cutover to the factory, with the maintainer. Reads the repository's GitHub issues once and maps the legacy pipeline's label vocabulary (factory:*, preview:*, scout:*, intake origins) onto factory issues (open ones, plus closed ones carrying a preview label or an intake origin) with their timeline rows and draft waits, holds a sitting where the maintainer confirms every pause, and imports only on the maintainer's explicit go.

name: landing-pull-requests
description: Land stage. Use when the Land routine takes the next In review issue of its pipe, for one judging round on its PR head (judge, then merge or fixer), or to close an issue whose every linked PR is merged.

name: measuring-the-factory
description: Use when the Maintenance routine runs, nightly. Exports issues, status history, timeline rows, pull requests, run costs and deploys with your own tools, runs measure.mjs on the export, and writes every row it prints as a factory snapshot. You never compute or correct a number yourself.

name: operating-the-factory
description: Use when the Maintenance routine runs, every 15 minutes. Catches what slipped through the structure - broken invariants, gestures or a repository's `notes` written by an agent, waits with no active owner, double or looping leases, self-verification, idle or dropped pull requests, a red target branch, piled-up Décisions, failing routines, unhealthy repositories, a stalled delivery chain, a blown budget - and answers each with one listed action or a Décision.

name: pr
description: Use when writing a PR body.

name: previewing-features
description: Use when screening routes a feature to preview, or a ruling resumes one at preview. Weighs the feature's durable value against its durable debt, writes the verdict candidate, park or reject as a preview row, and stops on a Decision for the maintainer's approval.

name: pruning-tests
description: Use when the Maintenance routine sweeps a repository's test suite, when a maintainer asks to audit a suite, or when an issue with origin scout:tests is executed. Scouts the tests whose time, flakiness or upkeep outweighs what they alone catch, audits every test of a suite for what it witnesses, or cuts one candidate, folding its lone assertion into a surviving test first.

name: releasing-downstream
description: Use when the Maintenance routine runs, on its hourly pass over the repositories other repositories consume. Finds a release not yet recorded, idempotent by sha and tag, and opens one release umbrella, one bump issue per consuming repository under it, and blocker waits on those bumps for the issues waiting on that release.

name: screening-issues
description: Use when the Screening routine takes the next issue of its pipe, on a ruling, a person's release, a new issue or a refresh, and on its Monday sweep. Re-resolves what the issue asserts against the target branch, closes what no longer holds, and routes the rest to Ready with an agent brief, to a launch, to preview or to a Decision.

name: setting-up-the-factory
description: Use when a person sets up Factory, adds a repository to it, changes its Slack channel, or asks why it skips a repository.

name: shaping-features
description: Use when a maintainer wants to choose what to shape next (the map of the open backlog), or when a feature idea, a family of issues, or an issue paused on a spec Task must become one approved spec, written to an umbrella issue with one task issue per change, chained by blockedBy. Runs live with the maintainer, never as a routine.

name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

name: triaging-issues
description: Use when a Screening run takes an issue whose `type` is empty or contradicted by a ruling. Classifies it as bug, enhancement, feature or chore from the issue's own text, keeps the reporter's cause as a hypothesis, and stops for a person when the text cannot settle the type.

name: waking-issues
description: Use when the Maintenance routine runs, on an issue set Done, a ruling recorded, or its hourly pass, which also reads every Task done or deleted and every merged or closed pull request. It is the only skill that resolves waits, applies a person's answers, wakes paused issues, and closes issues from their pull requests.

name: working-on-issues
description: Contract of every factory run. Use when a routine takes the next issue of its pipe, claims or releases it, stops for a person, writes a timeline row, or reads a repository's rules.

name: writing-plans
description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
